# Goal

We test whether **fine-tuning InfluPaint on RSV** beats **training a diffusion
model from scratch on RSV** ("RSVpaint"), and how much that gap depends on **how
much RSV data** the model sees. Both models treat an epidemic season as an image
(weeks x locations) and learn to generate plausible season trajectories.
Inpainting then conditions those images on the weeks we have already observed,
which turns them into forecasts.

To compare the two fairly we:

1. Hold out the latest season (2025-26) so no model sees it in training. This
   held-out slice is also what we send to Yue/Emily for evaluation.
2. Build training pools that vary one thing at a time: the amount of real
   surveillance data (100% / 50% / 25%), plus synthetic-only and all-data
   references. Source ratios are kept as even as the integer frame counts allow.
3. Train each pool two ways: `scratch` (a fresh diffusion model, "RSVpaint") and
   `finetune` (start from a trained flu InfluPaint checkpoint).
4. Score every model on the held-out season.

---

# Training data at a glance

A **frame** is one season-image: 53 weeks x states for one (source, season,
trajectory). Surveillance sources give one frame per season; the Scenario
Modelling Hub gives many synthetic trajectories per season.

**All RSV data available** (`RSV_FILLED.parquet`):

| Source    | Kind                                            | Seasons present                      | Frames |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------:|
| NHSN      | surveillance, hosp. admissions, all 51 states   | 2023, 2024, 2025                     | 3      |
| NSSP      | surveillance, ED-visit proportion, all states   | 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025               | 4      |
| RSV-Net   | surveillance, lab-confirmed hosp., ~14 states   | 2018-2025 (8 seasons)                | 8      |
| RSV_SMH   | synthetic, Scenario Modelling Hub               | 2023 (1600), 2024 (1500), 2025 (700) | 3800   |

Totals: **15 surveillance frames + 3800 synthetic frames**. Seasons are named by
start year (2025 = the 2025-26 season).

**After holding out the validation season** (season 2025, all sources), training
sees:

| Source              | Training seasons | Frames |
|---------------------|------------------|-------:|
| NHSN                | 2023, 2024       | 2      |
| NSSP                | 2022, 2023, 2024 | 3      |
| RSV-Net             | 2018-2024        | 7      |
| **Surveillance**    |                  | **12** |
| RSV_SMH (synthetic) | 2023, 2024       | 3100   |

So the **real surveillance pool the experiment varies is exactly 12 frames**.

---

# The models we train

Eight models. Everything is held fixed (architecture `scn868`, 64x64 images,
batch size 512) except the training pool and the initialisation.

| Model              | Init     | Training pool                       | Frames | Epochs |
|--------------------|----------|-------------------------------------|-------:|-------:|
| RSVpaint-100S      | scratch  | surveillance 100%                   | 12     | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-50S       | scratch  | surveillance 50%                    | 6      | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-25S       | scratch  | surveillance 25%                    | 3      | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-100M      | scratch  | synthetic only                      | 3100   | 3000   |
| RSVpaint-100A      | scratch  | all data (30% surv + 70% synthetic) | mixed  | 3000   |
| InfluPaint-ft-100S | finetune | surveillance 100%                   | 12     | 500    |
| InfluPaint-ft-50S  | finetune | surveillance 50%                    | 6      | 500    |
| InfluPaint-ft-25S  | finetune | surveillance 25%                    | 3      | 500    |

**The surveillance ladder (100S / 50S / 25S) is the core experiment.** We take
the 12 surveillance frames and keep 100%, 50%, or 25% of them, always keeping the
most-recent seasons and never dropping a source (NHSN must stay in: it is the
signal we condition on and score against at inference).

| Mix  | NHSN | NSSP | RSV-Net | Frames | x180 |
|------|-----:|-----:|--------:|-------:|-----:|
| 100S | 2    | 3    | 7       | 12     | 2160 |
| 50S  | 1    | 2    | 3       | 6      | 1080 |
| 25S  | 1    | 1    | 1       | 3      | 540  |

Every frame is replicated 180 times, so each pool clears the 512 batch size
(2160 / 1080 / 540 samples). The multiplier (180) and the epoch count (3000) are
identical across the ladder, so every frame gets the same exposure regardless of
pool size. The only difference between 100S and 50S is that half the unique
frames are missing, which is what makes "how much data" a clean variable.
Replicated copies are not identical: the mixer fills each copy's missing states
with random real surveillance, and training adds augmentation (Poisson noise,
time shifts), so the 180 copies never look the same to the model.

**Reference pools.** `100M` is synthetic only, used as-is (3100 frames, no
oversampling): does synthetic data alone work? `100A` mixes surveillance and
synthetic to a fixed 2160 total (30% surveillance + 70% synthetic): does adding
synthetic to surveillance help?

**Initialisation.** `scratch` starts from random weights (RSVpaint). `finetune`
starts from a trained flu InfluPaint checkpoint and keeps training on RSV. The
finetune arms mirror the surveillance ladder, so finetune-versus-scratch differs
only in initialisation. Finetune uses 500 epochs rather than 3000 because it
starts from already-trained weights.

# Scripts

Every step maps to one script in this `RSV/workflow/` folder. Run from the repo
root (`/Users/cy/.../influpaint/`).

| Step | Script                              | What it does |
|------|-------------------------------------|--------------|
| 1    | `validation_split.R`                | Drops the held-out season; saves train + validation parquets. |
| 2    | `build_training_sets.py`            | Builds one `.nc` training file per mix (100S, 50S, 25S, 100M, 100A). |
| 3    | `workflow.qmd` (this file)          | Inspects a built dataset. |
| 4    | `train_rsv.run` + `rsv_training.py` | SLURM submits one training job per model. |
| 5    | `rsv_inpaint.py`                    | Inpaints one checkpoint into a Hubverse forecast CSV (+ raw draws). |
| 6    | `plot_forecasts_validation.py`      | State-level forecast-versus-truth figure, one per model. |

---

# Step 1: Hold out the validation season

Split `RSV_FILLED.parquet` into a training file (held-out season removed) and a
validation file (only the held-out season).

We hold out **season 2025 (2025-26)**: train on the past, forecast the most
recent season. The split filters every source (NSSP, RSV-Net, NHSN, RSV_SMH) by
season, so even synthetic trajectories for that year are excluded and nothing
leaks. Edit `VALIDATION_SEASONS` at the top of `validation_split.R` to change it.

```{bash}
Rscript RSV/workflow/validation_split.R
```

This writes `RSV/data/RSV_TRAIN.parquet` (what models may see) and
`RSV/data/RSV_VALIDATION.parquet` (what Yue/Emily get). The printed report should show
12 surveillance frames in training (NHSN 2, NSSP 3, RSV-Net 7).

---

# Step 2: Build the training datasets

Turn `RSV_TRAIN.parquet` into one 4D tensor (saved as `.nc`) per mix, ready for
PyTorch. Each `.nc` file is a stack of season-images: a 64x64 grid where rows are
weeks (1-53, padded to 64) and columns are locations (padded to 64), and each
pixel is an incidence value.

The recipes live at the top of `build_training_sets.py`. `SURVEILLANCE_LADDER` defines three training sets built only from real surveillance data — 100S, 50S, and 25S — that differ only in how much history they include. These are nested: `select_recent_seasons` builds each smaller set by keeping only the most-recent seasons of each source, so 25S is a subset of 50S, which is a subset of 100S. Each step down just removes whole seasons which lets us measure the effect of historical exposure alone (see "The models we train"). Separately, `REFERENCE_POOLS` defines two synthetic-based mixes, 100M (pure model output) and 100A (a 70% model / 30% surveillance blend).

```{bash}
PYTHONPATH=. python RSV/workflow/build_training_sets.py \
    --input RSV/data/RSV_TRAIN.parquet \
    --outdir training_datasets \
    --tag 2026-06-23
```

This writes `training_datasets/RSV_<mix>_2026-06-23.nc` for each mix. The `--tag`
is what the SLURM scripts look for, so keep it consistent. To rebuild one mix while iterating, add `--only 100S`.

---

# Step 3: Inspect a built dataset

Open one `.nc` file and sanity-check its contents.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

from influpaint.utils import SeasonAxis, plotting as idplots

season_setup = SeasonAxis.for_flusight(remove_us=True, remove_territories=True)

# Edit this path to whichever mix you want to inspect
arr = xr.open_dataarray("training_datasets/RSV_100S_2026-06-23.nc")

print("Shape (samples, features, weeks, places):", arr.shape)
print("Mix config used:", arr.attrs["mix_cfg"])
print("First 5 origins :", arr.attrs["main_origins"][:5])
```

Plot a few trajectories on the US state grid. Each should look like a realistic
RSV season: a winter rise, a peak around December to February, and a decline.

```{python}
fig, ax = idplots.plot_us_grid(
    data=arr,
    season_axis=season_setup,
    sample_idx=list(np.arange(0, 5 * 17, step=17)),
    multi_line=True,
    sharey=False,
)
```

If anything looks off (wrong axes, all zeros, wildly different scales), fix it
before spending cluster time.

---

# Step 4: Train on Longleaf

Submit one SLURM job per model; each runs `rsv_training.py` on one L40 GPU. Two
pieces do the work:

- `rsv_training.py` is the entry point. Given a `.nc` file, a scenario ID (which
  fixes the U-Net and diffusion shape), and optionally a checkpoint to start
  from, it trains one model and logs everything to MLflow.
- `train_rsv.run` is the SLURM script. Its `RUN_TABLE` lists the 8 models; each
  row is one array task.

The scenario ID is fixed to `868` across every run so the architectures match.
That is what makes finetuning legal: flu InfluPaint weights only load into a
model of the same shape.

| Run tag         | Mix  | Mode     | Epochs |
|-----------------|------|----------|-------:|
| `100S_scratch`  | 100S | scratch  | 3000   |
| `50S_scratch`   | 50S  | scratch  | 3000   |
| `25S_scratch`   | 25S  | scratch  | 3000   |
| `100M_scratch`  | 100M | scratch  | 3000   |
| `100A_scratch`  | 100A | scratch  | 3000   |
| `100S_finetune` | 100S | finetune | 500    |
| `50S_finetune`  | 50S  | finetune | 500    |
| `25S_finetune`  | 25S  | finetune | 500    |

Scratch runs use 3000 epochs (an earlier attempt at 300 for the small mixes did
not converge: 1-4 batches per epoch over 300 epochs is too few gradient steps).
Finetune mode loads only the model weights from `FLUPAINT_CKPT`, not the optimiser
state (loading a foreign optimiser state makes the loss blow up to the millions);
a fresh optimiser is essential, controlled by `weights_only=True` in
`rsv_training.py`.

Before you submit, edit `train_rsv.run`:

- `DATE_TAG` must match the `--tag` from step 2.
- `FLUPAINT_CKPT` must point to a readable InfluPaint checkpoint on Longleaf
  (same scenario ID as `SCN_ID`).
- `REPO_ROOT` and `PYTHON` must match your Longleaf account (the script exports
  `PYTHONPATH=$REPO_ROOT` so the package imports).
- `EXPERIMENT_NAME` is the MLflow experiment; change it for a new round.

### Log in to Longleaf

1. Sign into Cisco AnyConnect VPN with your UNC credentials.
2. SSH in and grab an interactive GPU node:

```bash
ssh cgeisma1@longleaf.unc.edu
srun -p jlessler --gres=gpu:1 --mem=64G --time=10:00:00 --nodelist="g1803jles01" --pty /bin/zsh
```

3. Transfer the `.nc` files and repo from your local machine:

```bash
rsync -avz --progress \
  "/Users/cy/Documents/PROJECTS LOCAL/influpaint/training_datasets/RSV_"*"_2026-06-23.nc" \
  cgeisma1@longleaf.unc.edu:/proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint/training_datasets/
```

Check they arrived: `ls training_datasets/RSV_*_2026-06-23.nc`.

### Smoke-test before the real submission

Before burning cluster time, run 2 epochs in the interactive GPU job to confirm
the dataset loads and the loss drops. Make the package importable first (once per
shell session):

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint:$PYTHONPATH
python RSV/workflow/rsv_training.py \
    --dataset-nc training_datasets/RSV_100S_2026-06-23.nc \
    --scn-id 868 \
    --experiment-name rsv-smoketest \
    --run-tag smoketest \
    --epochs 2 \
    --batch-size 64 \
    --outdir /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/results/
```

If a `.pth` appears and MLflow shows a curve, the full submission is safe.

### Submit the array

```bash
cd /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint
sbatch RSV/workflow/train_rsv.run
# resubmit specific tasks after a failure, e.g. tasks 2 and 5:
# sbatch --array=2,5 RSV/workflow/train_rsv.run
```

Each job saves its checkpoint under `OUTDIR/<git_hash>_<experiment>_<date>/`
(set `OUTDIR` in `train_rsv.run`). MLflow keeps loss curves and sample plots.

### Monitor

Each task writes two logs:

- `slurm-<jobid>_<task>.out`: bash output (the `=== SLURM array task N ===`
  header). Failures before Python starts land here.
- `out_rsv_<experiment>_<run_tag>.out`: Python stdout. Loss curves, tracebacks,
  the final `Done. Checkpoint: ...` line.

```bash
squeue -u cgeisma1                                    # active jobs (PD pending, R running)
sacct -u cgeisma1 -j <jobid> --format=JobID,JobName,State,ExitCode,Elapsed
tail -f out_rsv_rsv-2026-06-23_100S_scratch.out       # watch one run
scancel <jobid>_5 <jobid>_6                           # cancel specific tasks
grep "Done. Checkpoint" out_rsv_rsv-2026-06-23_*.out  # scan for finished runs
```

### Consolidate checkpoints

The git hash changes between submissions, so the 8 checkpoints end up scattered
across a few `results/` folders. Gather them into one place:

```bash
mkdir -p /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/
cp /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/results/*/{scratch,finetune}_*_scn868_ep*.pth \
   /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/
ls -lh /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/
```

You should end up with 8 `.pth` files, the inputs to step 5.

### Inspect training quality

Two helpers turn the per-run outputs into PNGs you can preview in VSCode. Both
take no arguments; edit the path constants at the top of each if yours differ.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD   # plot_samples_curves.py imports the influpaint package

# Loss curves for every run (log y-axis); globs out_rsv_*.out in the cwd
python RSV/workflow/plot_losses.py            # -> rsv_training_losses.png

# Per-checkpoint sample curves vs held-out truth; globs every checkpoint in
# CHECKPOINTS_DIR and finds its samples under results/
python RSV/workflow/plot_samples_curves.py    # -> <ckpt>_curves.png + rsv_samples_curves.pdf
```

# Step 5: Inpaint the held-out season (forecasting)

Take one trained checkpoint, fill in the unobserved weeks of the held-out season,
and write the result as a Hubverse CSV (the shape you would submit to the CDC RSV
Forecast Hub).

How it works: the model learned to draw a whole RSV season as a 64x64 image
(rows = weeks, columns = states). We paint in the weeks we have already observed,
lock those pixels, and let the model fill in the rest. The filled-in part is the
forecast. We draw `batch_size` independent fills, so the spread across draws
gives the forecast quantiles.

The script is `rsv_inpaint.py`. Two things make it RSV-specific:

1. **Scaling must match training.** A diffusion model works on normalised
   numbers, so reading its output back as real RSV values means undoing that
   normalisation with the same scaling used in training. That scaling comes from
   the training `.nc` file, so pass the same-mix `.nc` the checkpoint was trained
   on (`finetune_100S_*.pth` uses `RSV_100S_<tag>.nc`). A different mix's `.nc`
   silently rescales every forecast.
2. **Ground truth is the held-out parquet, not a flu hub.** It is built with
   `GroundTruth.from_rsv(...)` from one surveillance signal (default `NHSN`,
   hospital admission counts, which reports all states) for the held-out season.
   The chosen signal is used both as the weeks we condition on and as the weeks
   we score against, so the forecast comes out in that signal's units.

**Mask and horizon convention.** `--reference-date` is a Saturday. Weeks ending
before it are known; horizon 0 is the reference week itself (the first unobserved
week), and Hubverse horizons 0, 1, 2, 3 are emitted, with
`target_end_date = reference_date + 7 x horizon`. The target is `wk inc rsv hosp`
(NHSN hospitalisations). We drop the hub's `-1` backcast: on final held-out data
it is a week we already observed and locked into the model, so it carries no
forecast information.

**Why NHSN and not RSV-Net.** The ground-truth signal is used both to condition on
and to score against, so coverage matters. NHSN reports all 51 states, giving a
complete conditioning image. RSV-Net reports only ~14 states, which would force
the other ~37 to zero in the known weeks and mislead the model about where RSV is.
`NSSP` (target `wk inc rsv prop ed visits`) is the other full-coverage option if
you want ED-visit proportion instead of hospitalisations.

### Smoke-test (one checkpoint, one date)

On Longleaf, in an interactive GPU job, from the repo root:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
python RSV/workflow/rsv_inpaint.py \
    --checkpoint /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/checkpoints/finetune_100S_finetune_scn868_ep500.pth \
    --dataset-nc training_datasets/RSV_100S_2026-06-23.nc \
    --reference-date 2025-12-20 \
    --signal NHSN \
    --season 2025 \
    --outdir RSV/forecasts_validation
```

This writes `RSV/forecasts_validation/2025-12-20-UNC_IDD-InfluPaint-RSV.csv` and
the raw draws (`2025-12-20_draws_ti.npy`). Plot it with step 6: the median should
track the observed curve up to the reference date and fan out afterwards.
Forecasts orders of magnitude off the observed line usually mean a `--dataset-nc`
that does not match the checkpoint's mix.

### Scale up

Once the smoke-test looks right, forecast the whole season for every model. On
Longleaf this is the `inpaint_rsv.run` array job (8 models x 18 reference weeks =
144 tasks):

```bash
cd /proj/jlessler/projects/influpaint_general/influpaint_RSV/influpaint
sbatch RSV/workflow/inpaint_rsv.run
```

Hand the CSVs to Yue for scoring against `RSV_VALIDATION.parquet`.

---

# Step 6: Plot forecast versus truth

After the sweep, render one state-level figure per model:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
python RSV/workflow/plot_forecasts_validation.py
# -> RSV/forecasts_validation/<MODEL>/<MODEL>_forecast_validation.png
```

Each figure is two rows over four states (North Carolina, New York, Texas,
Florida). The top row shows the 4-week-ahead forecasts (horizons 0-3) at several
reference dates; the bottom row shows the full-season forecasts with a few example
trajectories. Black is the observed NHSN truth, and each reference date gets its
own colour (shared across both rows). Quantiles and trajectories come from the 512
conditional draws in each `*_draws_ti.npy`; ground truth is rebuilt with
`GroundTruth.from_rsv` on the held-out NHSN parquet, so truth and forecast align
by construction.

Useful flags: `--model RSVpaint-100S` (one model), `--states NC NY TX FL`,
`--n-refs 5` (reference dates shown), `--n-traj 10` (trajectories per date), and
`--xlim-start` / `--xlim-end` (season window).
